findings.body: After close writes a clean receipt, rerunning a check on the same commit and failing it leaves this row at `stage: "ready"`, even after the checks cache expires and `pr.checks` becomes `fail`. `_item_readiness` trusts the matching receipt without considering the fresh check result, and `_item` also continues advertising the merge step (src/forge/nextstep.py:576–588). This is new evidence beyond the ruling about retaining receipt-based readiness when GitHub is unavailable: here GitHub supplies a known failure. Reconcile readiness and the item's next step with known failed or running checks, while preserving the ruled unavailable-data fallback, and cover this scenario through the commands.
findings.title: Not done: report readiness when checks fail after a successful close

findings.body: The previously reported gap remains. `upgrade.release_notice` returns its announcement before the state report (src/forge/upgrade.py:186–187), and `machine_next` selects the first non-Next line. When an upgrade exists, a waiting item or human-only merge therefore gets the release announcement as `next.line`, hiding its actual state. Build the machine next object from `_report`'s lines and keep the release notice separate.
findings.title: Keep release notices from replacing next.line

findings.body: The machine board recognizes merged tasks and fixes only from state files already present on the fetched default branch. Both PR lookups contain only open PRs, and story next-step calculation receives an empty merged-PR set here. After a human merges on GitHub, but before a fetch, the board consequently retains the old stage and merge/close instruction. The text next report already handles this through its merged-PR lookup (src/forge/nextstep.py:187–188). Reuse that evidence for task and fix stages and story next-step calculation so the machine command does not depend on a subsequent fetch to recognize the merge.
findings.title: Recognize GitHub merges before the default branch is fetched

stop.done: src/forge/board.py is simpler and behaves as it did before
